trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
The line must go right: up is number 10, which comes later; left is number 7, which comes later; down is number 8, which comes later.
I can't rule out up, right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
Going left would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes around the edge to (5,4).
Cell (4,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Going up would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes down.
Going around the edge to (5,1) would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes around the edge to (1,5).

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going around the edge to (1,1), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,5). So my guess (up from cell (3,4)) was wrong, so the line must go right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going around the edge to (3,1), the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,4). So my guess (up from cell (4,3)) was wrong. Next I'll try right.
Going down, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,1). So the line goes up.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
Going left, the next 9 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,1). So the line goes around the edge to (5,4).
Going left would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going around the edge to (5,1) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
The line must go up: around the edge to (4,1) is number 7, which comes later.
Going around the edge to (3,1) would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Going around the edge to (2,1) would strand number 5: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (1,1).
Going around the edge to (5,1) would force the line onto number 7 before its turn; going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,2). So the line goes right.
Going right would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
The line must go left: right is number 9, which comes later; down is number 10, which comes later.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
